entry.title: Verhoogde Tegemoetkoming(Increased Reimbursemnet)
entry.content:
0. Introduction

For an international student study in Leuven, Vlaams, Belgium. Getting insured in Belgium does not goes so smooth like how you would pay for you meal - it would take you month, even a quarter until everything is set and you get your money back. The good news is, Belgium is considered one of the most low-cost countries in terms of health care and the service they get. The bad news is, it’s quite tricky and goes through lots of burecracy process that would just keep you waiting. And in case if you are not insured w/ anything, you would probably not go bankrupted like the US styple, but it would definitely makes you wallets much thinner.

So this is largely based on my personal experience, after spending nearly thousand euros in wrongful health insurance companies and uninsured Emergency Room/GP visit/pills, I come these as my expereiences. We need to talk about what I believe probably the most important part in Belgium Welfare System:

Verhoogde Tegemoetkoming

Below are guidance mainly summarised and generated by GPT-5-pro via web research, and I made modifications based on its output.

What is “Verhoogde Tegemoetkoming” (VT)?

Belgium’s “you-earn-less-so-healthcare-costs-you-less” status. If you have VT, doctor visits, meds and hospital stays are way cheaper - in gerenal speaking, it will be ~70% less than typical insurance and ~95% less than uninsured case; you only pay the copay (e.g., visit GP is €0-1). Think of it as a discount card issued by your health fund (mutualiteit).

Of course there’s a limit cap for the “low-income-person”, but if you are a student status not working full time in the same time, you will probably not reach that threadshold so don’t worry to much on it.

A pretty nice video intro on how to get it can be found in Youtbe, credit to @Amal

1. What VT changes within the Health Insurance

We will only cover the case w/ CM insurance(cuz that’s the one I am insured with and the only company that I know about XD)

GP consultations (geconventioneerde GP)

  • You pay only the small co‑pay (remgeld); the rest is billed to the fund via the third‑party payer. VT patients have a right to this at the GP. (RIZIV)

  • Examples:

    • GP consult with GMD (globaal medisch dossier): €1.00 remgeld with VT (vs €4.00 without VT).
    • GP consult without GMD: €1.50 remgeld with VT (vs €6.00 without VT). (CM)

Psychological care (two layers)

  • Publicly funded first‑line psychology (RIZIV networks): for adults ≥24 y the personal share is €4 per session with VT (vs €11). See CM’s explanation of network‑based care. (CM)
  • CM’s extra member benefit (outside the network): CM refunds part of sessions with recognised clinicians; for children & youth CM states 50% up to €30 per session, or 75% up to €45 per session if you have VT (up to lifetime caps). (CM)

Medicines & contraception

  • VT leads to higher reimbursement across many reimbursable medicines (lower remgeld). RIZIV confirms an extra reimbursement for contraceptives for people ≤24 years or with VT regardless of age/gender (morning‑after pill is reimbursed for everyone). (RIZIV)

Hospitalisation: lower personal shares + CM top‑ups for VT

  • RIZIV confirms that a patient’s personal share (co‑pay) depends on status, and VT reduces what you pay. (RIZIV)
  • CM details the fixed hospital forfaits where VT pays less or nothing; e.g., forfait medical imaging co‑pay is €1.98 with VT (vs €6.20), forfait technical procedures per admission is €0 with VT, and per‑day hospital medicines forfait is €0 with VT. (CM)
  • CM extra support if you have VT and no hospital insurance: CM pays 75% of the legally defined personal shares (room, medical/paramedical fees, and top‑ups on reimbursable medicines). This is a CM‑specific complementary benefit. (CM)

Maximumfactuur (MAF): yearly cap on copay

  • Belgium’s Maximumfactuur(Maximum Amount) caps a family’s annual co‑pays; with VT you benefit from the “social MAF” at a lower cap. For 2025, social MAF is €527.27; if a chronic‑care trigger is met, the cap drops to €410.10 (HZIV)
  • General info pages on MAF from Vlaanderen.be and CM explain how caps apply and that VT households can be treated as a separate “VT‑sub‑family” for the social MAF. (Vlaanderen.be)

2. Other deductions on tickets, fees etc.

Public transport (student‑relevant)

  • De Lijn (Flanders): with VT you are entitled to a reduced‑rate annual pass (Buzzy Pazz 6–24y or Omnipas 25–64y). Discount is applied automatically when buying/renewing online or at a point of sale (they check your VT via the national register). De Lijn’s pages list the VT discount and automatic processing. (De Lijn)
  • NMBS/SNCB (trains): VT holders get 50% off standard tickets with the VT discount (via a specific entitlement loaded and checked at purchase). See NMBS’s discount overview and the “Large families, persons …” page on how the VT entitlement is verified. (NMBS announced a new fare structure earlier in 2025, but as of 30 Sep 2025 the official discount page still lists 50% for VT holders—check at purchase in case of updates.) (Belgian Train)
  • MIVB/STIB (Brussels): VT holders can buy the RVV pass at a reduced price—€8.10 per month or €85 per year (2025 page). ([STIB - MIVB][16])

Flemish “zorgpremie” (care premium) of the Vlaamse Sociale Bescherming

  • If you had VT on 1 Jan of the previous year, you pay the reduced zorgpremie. In 2025 the standard premium is €64; with VT it’s €32. (The Flemish government has indicated a general increase from 2026; but 2025 values are as stated here.) ([Departement Zorg][17])

Leuven‑specific municipal benefits connected to VT

  • Free UiTPAS (kansentarief) + 80% discount on partner culture/sport/leisure activities and membership/registration fees across Leuven, Bierbeek, Herent, Oud‑Heverlee. The city explicitly lists this under VT. ([Homepage Stad Leuven][18])
  • Free annual package of household waste bags if you have VT (city measure; see the Leuven page for details and the 2025 council decision). ([Homepage Stad Leuven][19])
  • The Leuven VT page also points to De Lijn/NMBS VT transport discounts, local support (e.g., energy coaching) and “Iedereen Verdient Vakantie” discounted trips. ([Homepage Stad Leuven][18])

Telecom/internet (important nuance)

  • Since 1 Mar 2024, Belgium runs a new “Sociaal internetaanbod”. Having VT by itself does not make you eligible (eligibility is based on other social criteria); official guidance is explicit on this point. ([Economie][20])

3. Special offers & KUL-student‑oriented extras

UiTPAS Leuven kansentarief

  • With a recent attest VT, Leuven grants a free UiTPAS and 80% discounts on tickets, membership and course fees at participating organisations in Leuven/Bierbeek/Herent/Oud‑Heverlee; great for cinema, community sports, cultural venues, workshops. See examples and application steps (accepts a VT attest not older than 3 months; annual auto‑renew where still eligible). ([Homepage Stad Leuven][21])

KU Leuven Sport – (partial) reimbursement via your mutuality

  • CM’s sports‑club benefit: up to €15 per person per year for membership at a sports club, sports centre/service, recognised jogging or swimming initiations, etc. You can apply this to (part of) your KU Leuven Sports Card or fitness subscription. ([CM][22])
  • KU Leuven Sports publishes the mutuality forms and explains the one‑time yearly reimbursement process (get the right CM form, have KU Leuven Sport stamp it, and submit to CM). ([KU Leuven][23])

CM student travel assistance for study abroad (Erasmus, etc.)

  • If you’re studying in another European country, CM’s student travel assistance gives access to the Mutas emergency centre and reimbursement for urgent medical costs abroad (complements your European Health Insurance Card). Notify CM before you go. ([CM][24])

A few other CM extras students often use

  • Vaccinations: certain vaccines are reimbursed by the compulsory insurance and CM; CM also documents travel‑vaccine reimbursements pathways (and via optional CM MediKo Plan). ([CM][25])
  • Eye care: if there’s no statutory reimbursement, CM pays €40/year towards a new pair of glasses as a member benefit (separate from optional insurances). ([CM][26])

Quick how‑to (claiming the main benefits)

  1. Check/obtain proof of VT In Mijn CM or request an Attest verhoogde tegemoetkoming (CM forms). You’ll need this for UiTPAS, sometimes for transport products. (CM)

  2. Use the third‑party payer at the GP As a VT patient, your GP must apply it; you pay only the remgeld (e.g., €1 with GMD). (RIZIV)

  3. Psychological care Prefer RIZIV network psychologists when possible (co‑pay €4 with VT), and use CM’s extra refunds where applicable (youth: up to 75%/€45 with VT). (CM)

  4. Public transport

    • De Lijn: buy or renew your Buzzy Pazz/Omnipas; the VT discount is applied automatically online once your national number is entered. ([help.delijn.be][27])
    • NMBS: ensure your VT entitlement is recognised at a ticket office or in your online profile to get 50% discount on tickets. (Belgian Train)
    • MIVB: buy the RVV subscription (listed price: €8.10/month or €85/year). ([STIB - MIVB][16])

  5. UiTPAS (Leuven region) Apply online or at a sales point with your VT attest (<3 months old) to get a free card and 80% discounts at partner organisations. ([Homepage | Stad Leuven][21])

  6. KU Leuven Sports Card reimbursement Download CM’s sports reimbursement form, get it stamped at KU Leuven Sport, and submit to CM (up to €15/year). ([CM][22])

  7. Keep an eye on your annual cap If your remgeld reaches the MAF cap (with VT usually €527.27 in 2025), the rest of that year’s eligible co‑pays are reimbursed automatically. (HZIV)

Notes, limits & recent changes to be aware of

  • Hospitalisation billing: choose common or two‑bed rooms and conventioned providers to avoid supplements; CM’s VT hospital top‑up (75% of personal shares if you lack hospital insurance) is exceptional but only covers legally defined personal shares. (CM)
  • NMBS discount rounding / tariff changes: NMBS announced a new fare structure in 2025; at the time of writing, the official page still shows 50% VT discount—verify at purchase in case of roll‑out changes. (Belgian Train)
  • Telecom: VT alone does not grant the new social internet offer; eligibility depends on other social criteria. ([Economie][20])
  • Flemish care premium: 2025 amounts are €64 standard / €32 with VT; Flemish sources indicate increases are planned from 2026—monitor when budgeting future years. ([Departement Zorg][17])

Sources (selection)

  • CM: Verhoogde Tegemoetkoming explainer and forms; GP 2025 tariffs (incl. €1/€1.50 remgeld with VT), hospitalization & hospital forfaits, psychological care (network co‑pays and youth VT amounts), sports club refund. (CM)
  • RIZIV/INAMI: VT concept; third‑party payer rule; contraceptive extra reimbursement list. (RIZIV)
  • MAF (Maximumfactuur) rules & 2025 caps (HZIV/Vlaanderen/CM). (HZIV)
  • Transport operators: De Lijn VT reduction & automatic processing; NMBS VT −50%; MIVB RVV €8.10/m or €85/y (2025). (De Lijn)
  • Leuven: City VT page consolidating local benefits (free UiTPAS kansentarief; free household bags; pointers to De Lijn/NMBS discounts). UiTPAS kansentarief details (80% discount). ([Homepage Stad Leuven][18])
  • Flemish care premium (zorgpremie): 2025 amounts and reduced rate with VT. ([Departement Zorg][17])

[16]: https://www.stib-mivb.be/kopen/abonnementen-voor-reizigers-met-beperkte-mobiliteit “ Abonnementen voor reizigers met beperkte mobiliteit - MIVB” [17]: https://www.departementzorg.be/nl/de-zorgpremie?utm_source=chatgpt.com “De zorgpremie | Departement Zorg” [18]: https://www.leuven.be/verhoogde-tegemoetkoming “Verhoogde tegemoetkoming | Stad Leuven” [19]: https://www.leuven.be/gratis-huisvuilzakken?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Gratis huisvuilzakken - Stad Leuven” [20]: https://economie.fgov.be/nl/themas/online/telecommunicatie/sociaal-internetaanbod-gunstig?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Sociaal internetaanbod: gunstig tarief voor vast internet” [21]: https://www.leuven.be/uitpas-met-kansentarief “UiTPAS met kansentarief | Stad Leuven” [22]: https://www.cm.be/nl/diensten-en-voordelen/sportvereniging?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Sportvereniging | CM” [23]: https://www.kuleuven.be/sport/aanbod/tussenkomst-in-het-lidgeld-van-een-sportclub-of-fitnessabonnement-via-uw-mutualiteit?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Tussenkomst in het lidgeld van een sportclub of … - KU Leuven” [24]: https://www.cm.be/nl/diensten-en-voordelen/reisbijstand-voor-studenten?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Reisbijstand voor studenten - CM” [25]: https://www.cm.be/nl/diensten-en-voordelen/vaccins-met-cm-terugbetaling?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Vaccins met CM-terugbetaling” [26]: https://www.cm.be/nl/diensten-en-voordelen/brillen?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Brillen - CM” [27]: https://help.delijn.be/hc/nl/articles/360039270852-Hoe-verleng-ik-mijn-abonnement?utm_source=chatgpt.com “Hoe verleng ik mijn abonnement? - Vragen & Contact”

entry.title: Pitch For Thesis Topic
entry.content:
I would like to start with describing my thesis project, and this will be the one that I intend to pitch, despite I haven’t started to work on it yet.

It’s about devloping a classification algorithm based on pharmarcy dispensing records, and we focus on one-specific type of disease – diabetes patients.

Outlet Choice

Let’s suppose this research project has been successfully completed, and the corresponding essay has been published after harsh peer review. Now, We aim to share this work with the general public.

The first one to reach out will be Casey Ross, a reporter with special focus and specialize in health AI. He cares about the AI safetly and real-world impact on care delivery, which makes him a perfect initial contact as we try to expand my research to clinicians and policy makers through his report.

Message Box

  • Issue: The current approach to diabete care is passive, only addressing problems after they have already developed.
  • Problem: Diabete Patients record are heterogenous, i.e. every patient is unique.
  • Benefits: This allows doctors to give personalized care to the patients who need it most before they get sicker.
  • So what: Fewer emergency room visits, saving money for the government and improve the quality of life for patients.
  • Solution: We use novel modelling technqiues to predict their future behavior, based on pharmarcy records.

Pitch Email

Dear Casy Ross,

We are researchers from KU Leuven and Itec-imec. Your insightful coverage in patient care resonates deeply with a critical issue in diabetes management: a one-size-fits-all approach that too often leads patients into costly complications.

Our recent study offers a way to preempt this. By digging into underutilized pharmacy dispensing records w/ novel survival tree models, we can track each patient’s adherence trajectories over time.

This isn’t just another predictive model — it’s a validated method to identify and intervene with the highest-risk patients before hospitalization becomes necessary. It offers a concrete step beyond today’s current, reactive approach.

You can find details on this website:

  • xxxxxxxxxthere-is-supposed-to-be-a-websitexxxxxxxxxxx .

We have a summary and are willing to discuss w/ you how this approach could rewrite the playbook for managing chronic disease.

Thank you for considering our work and looking forward to your reply.

Best regards,

Xinyu Yang

Challenges

This may face follwing criticism:

  • Classified as spam email, and be ghosted. No reply at all.
  • “This sounds like more AI hype. We see dozens of these ‘predictive model’ papers. What makes this one different?”
  • “What’s truly novel about the methodology? Others have used machine learning on diabetes data for years.”
  • “How reliable is pharmacy dispensing data? It doesn’t capture everything, and patients could just be stockpiling medication.”

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation: putting AI Giants in Your Pocket

link.title: Knowledge Distillation: putting AI Giants in Your Pocket

entry.content:
Introduction

Imagine you’re a great chef :cook: with a special recipe you’ve worked on for many years. Your helper wants to learn from you, but the recipe is complicated. Instead of teaching every tiny step, you share the main points in a simple way. This approach to teaching complex concepts is similar to what we call model distillation in Artificial Intelligence (AI).

Just as alcohol distillation isn’t about reducing volume, but about purifying a substance, model distillation isn’t simply shrinking models, but a process of extracting and transferring knowledge.

Why is Model Distillation Important?

Most AI models are huge, with trillions (like millions of millions) of parameters. These big models, like the ones used for apps like ChatGPT, are very smart but difficult to run on regular laptops because they need a lot of power. Model distillation lets us shrink these big models into smaller ones that can run easily on everyday devices.

Don't be fooled by size!

In the left picture, we can see
  • The teacher model is Deepseek-R1-0528, one of the frontier models.
  • The distilled model is Deepseek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B, being 100 times smaller than the teacher model, and can be deployed in a PC.
  • Despite being significantly smaller, Deepseek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B still achieves good performance, even compared to other frontier models.

Also, because the student model is small, it needs much less electricity to think(great for the earth!). Smaller also means cheaper, so more people can play with it on laptops and even cellphones instead of mega-servers that cover areas comparable to football stadiums.

Knowledge Distillation Process

How Does Large Model Distillation Work?

It's inspired by the chemical distillation process and has the following parallel relationship:

  • Chemical distillation: :test_tube: Mixed substance → :fire: Heating → :dash: Vaporization → :snowflake: Cooling → :droplet: Pure liquid
  • Model distillation: :teacher: Large model → :gear: Training → :bulb: Knowledge extraction → :arrows_counterclockwise: Conversion → :student: Small model

Here’s what it means for each step:

  • Teacher AI Model 🧑‍🏫: This is a big AI model, like ChatGPT, that knows a lot and gives very detailed answers.
  • Student AI Model 🎓: This is a smaller model made to work quickly on phones and computers.
  • Training and Knowledge Transfer 🔄: The teacher AI looks at lots of data and gives the correct answers and explains why these answers are correct.
  • Learning Process 📚: The student AI learns both the correct answers and the reasoning behind them. This helps the student AI give good answers even though it is smaller.

Take-away: Distillation is an Apprenticeship

Model distillation is like an apprenticeship, where the student learns directly from the teacher, step by step. Just as an apprentice chef learns cooking skills by watching and following closely as the experienced chef prepares dishes, the smaller AI model learns key concepts directly from the larger, knowledgeable AI model.

Conclusion

Through model distillation, we demonstrate a way to make Large AI models more accessible, efficient, and widely usable, not just those with access to massive computing resources.

entry.title: Google Gemini updates: Flash 1.5, Gemma 2 and Project Astra

link.title: Google Gemini updates: Flash 1.5, Gemma 2 and Project Astra

entry.content:
May 14, 2024 We’re introducing a series of updates across the Gemini family of models, including the new 1.5 Flash, our lightweight model for speed and efficiency, and Project Astra, our vision for the future of AI assistants. In December, we launched our first natively multimodal model Gemini 1.0 in three sizes: Ultra, Pro and Nano. Just a few months later we released 1.5 Pro, with enhanced performance and a breakthrough long context window of 1 million tokens.Developers and enterprise customers have been putting 1.5 Pro to use in incredible ways and finding its long context window, multimodal reasoning capabilities and impressive overall performance incredibly useful.We know from user feedback that some applications need lower latency and a lower cost to serve. This inspired us to keep innovating, so today, we’re introducing Gemini 1.5 Flash: a model that’s lighter-weight than 1.5 Pro, and designed to be fast and efficient to serve at scale.Both 1.5 Pro and 1.5 Flash are available in public preview with a 1 million token context window in Google AI Studio and Vertex AI. And now, 1.5 Pro is also available with a 2 million token context window via waitlist to developers using the API and to Google Cloud customers.We’re also introducing updates across the Gemini family of models, announcing our next generation of open models, Gemma 2, and sharing progress on the future of AI assistants, with Project Astra.Context lengths of leading foundation models compared with Gemini 1.5’s 2 million token capability1.5 Flash is the newest addition to the Gemini model family and the fastest Gemini model served in the API. It’s optimized for high-volume, high-frequency tasks at scale, is more cost-efficient to serve and features our breakthrough long context window.While it’s a lighter weight model than 1.5 Pro, it’s highly capable of multimodal reasoning across vast amounts of information and delivers impressive quality for its size.The new Gemini 1.5 Flash model is optimized for speed and efficiency, is highly capable of multimodal reasoning and features our breakthrough long context window.1.5 Flash excels at summarization, chat applications, image and video captioning, data extraction from long documents and tables, and more. This is because it’s been trained by 1.5 Pro through a process called “distillation,” where the most essential knowledge and skills from a larger model are transferred to a smaller, more efficient model.Read more about 1.5 Flash in our updated Gemini 1.5 technical report, on the Gemini technology page, and learn about 1.5 Flash’s availability and pricing.Over the last few months, we’ve significantly improved 1.5 Pro, our best model for general performance across a wide range of tasks.Beyond extending its context window to 2 million tokens, we’ve enhanced its code generation, logical reasoning and planning, multi-turn conversation, and audio and image understanding through data and algorithmic advances. We see strong improvements on public and internal benchmarks for each of these tasks.1.5 Pro can now follow increasingly complex and nuanced instructions, including ones that specify product-level behavior involving role, format and style. We’ve improved control over the model’s responses for specific use cases, like crafting the persona and response style of a chat agent or automating workflows through multiple function calls. And we’ve enabled users to steer model behavior by setting system instructions.We added audio understanding in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, so 1.5 Pro can now reason across image and audio for videos uploaded in Google AI Studio. And we’re now integrating 1.5 Pro into Google products, including Gemini Advanced and in Workspace apps.Read more about 1.5 Pro in our updated Gemini 1.5 technical report and on the Gemini technology page.Gemini Nano is expanding beyond text-only inputs to include images as well. Starting with Pixel, applications using Gemini Nano with Multimodality will be able to understand the world the way people do — not just through text, but also through sight, sound and spoken language.Read more about Gemini 1.0 Nano on Android.Today, we’re also sharing a series of updates to Gemma, our family of open models built from the same research and technology used to create the Gemini models.We’re announcing Gemma 2, our next generation of open models for responsible AI innovation. Gemma 2 has a new architecture designed for breakthrough performance and efficiency, and will be available in new sizes.The Gemma family is also expanding with PaliGemma, our first vision-language model inspired by PaLI-3. And we’ve upgraded our Responsible Generative AI Toolkit with LLM Comparator for evaluating the quality of model responses.Read more on the Developer blog.As part of Google DeepMind’s mission to build AI responsibly to benefit humanity, we’ve always wanted to develop universal AI agents that can be helpful in everyday life. That’s why today, we’re sharing our progress in building the future of AI assistants with Project Astra (advanced seeing and talking responsive agent).To be truly useful, an agent needs to understand and respond to the complex and dynamic world just like people do — and take in and remember what it sees and hears to understand context and take action. It also needs to be proactive, teachable and personal, so users can talk to it naturally and without lag or delay.While we’ve made incredible progress developing AI systems that can understand multimodal information, getting response time down to something conversational is a difficult engineering challenge. Over the past few years, we’ve been working to improve how our models perceive, reason and converse to make the pace and quality of interaction feel more natural.Building on Gemini, we’ve developed prototype agents that can process information faster by continuously encoding video frames, combining the video and speech input into a timeline of events, and caching this information for efficient recall.By leveraging our leading speech models, we also enhanced how they sound, giving the agents a wider range of intonations. These agents can better understand the context they’re being used in, and respond quickly, in conversation.With technology like this, it’s easy to envision a future where people could have an expert AI assistant by their side, through a phone or glasses. And some of these capabilities are coming to Google products, like the Gemini app and web experience, later this year.We’ve made incredible progress so far with our family of Gemini models, and we’re always striving to advance the state-of-the-art even further. By investing in a relentless production line of innovation, we’re able to explore new ideas at the frontier, while also unlocking the possibility of new and exciting Gemini use cases.Learn more about Gemini and its capabilities. Your information will be used in accordance with Google’s privacy policy.

entry.title: Analysis II Tutorial Notes
entry.content:
We choose to introduce metric spaces and normed vector spaces at the beginning of the course. Convergence is a concept that runs throughout all of analysis, and most convergence can be uniformly described using the language of metric spaces … This makes transitions to advanced topics such as continuity of multivariable functions, uniform convergence of function sequences, and even convergence in $\mathcal{L}^p$ spaces much more seamless. — Pin Yu

During the final semester of my undergraduate studies, I volunteered to tutor first-year students in Analysis. Instead of following the convoluted approach found in traditional Chinese textbooks, I presented these concepts through the lens of metric spaces. This perspective doesn’t add unnecessary abstraction, but rather provides clarity and unified approach.

Below are links to some of my previous tutorials (note: content is primarily in English with some Chinese, as it was developed for Chinese students):

  • Everything you need to know about spaces
    • Construction of abstract spaces
    • Understanding $| \cdot |_{\mathcal{L}^p}$ norm
    • Dual Space and Hölder’s inequality.
  • Introduction to Topology
    • Basic Concepts and insights on topology
    • Compactness = Completness + Totally Bounded Set
  • TBD

entry.title: Displaying External Posts on Your al-folio Blog

link.title: Displaying External Posts on Your al-folio Blog

entry.content:
External Posts on Your al-folio Blog

If you prefer publishing blog posts on medium.com or other external sources, starting version v0.5.0, al-folio lets you to display your external posts in the blog feed of your website! 🎉🎉

Configuring external sources of super simple. After upgrading to v0.5.0, just add the following section to your _config.yml:

external_sources:
  - name: medium.com  # name of the source (arbitrary string)
    rss_url: https://medium.com/@<your-medium-username>/feed

The example above adds your medium.com blog post feed as an external source. But you can add arbitrary RSS feeds as sources.

Any questions or suggestions? 👉 Start a discussion on GitHub!

entry.title: a post with math
entry.content:
This theme supports rendering beautiful math in inline and display modes using MathJax 3 engine. You just need to surround your math expression with $$, like $$ E = mc^2 $$. If you leave it inside a paragraph, it will produce an inline expression, just like \(E = mc^2\).

To use display mode, again surround your expression with $$ and place it as a separate paragraph. Here is an example:

\[\sum_{k=1}^\infty |\langle x, e_k \rangle|^2 \leq \|x\|^2\]

You can also use \begin{equation}...\end{equation} instead of $$ for display mode math. MathJax will automatically number equations:

\begin{equation} \label{eq:cauchy-schwarz} \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k b_k \right)^2 \leq \left( \sum_{k=1}^n a_k^2 \right) \left( \sum_{k=1}^n b_k^2 \right) \end{equation}

and by adding \label{...} inside the equation environment, we can now refer to the equation using \eqref.

Note that MathJax 3 is a major re-write of MathJax that brought a significant improvement to the loading and rendering speed, which is now on par with KaTeX.

This theme implements a built-in Jekyll feature, the use of Rouge, for syntax highlighting. It supports more than 100 languages. This example is in C++. All you have to do is wrap your code in markdown code tags:

```c++
code code code
```

int main(int argc, char const \*argv[])
{
    string myString;

    cout << "input a string: ";
    getline(cin, myString);
    int length = myString.length();

    char charArray = new char * [length];

    charArray = myString;
    for(int i = 0; i < length; ++i){
        cout << charArray[i] << " ";
    }

    return 0;
}

For displaying code in a list item, you have to be aware of the indentation, as stated in this Stackoverflow answer. You must indent your code by (3 * bullet_indent_level) spaces. This is because kramdown (the markdown engine used by Jekyll) indentation for the code block in lists is determined by the column number of the first non-space character after the list item marker. For example:

1. We can put fenced code blocks inside nested bullets, too.

   1. Like this:

      ```c
      printf("Hello, World!");
      ```

   2. The key is to indent your fenced block in the same line as the first character of the line.

Which displays:

  1. We can put fenced code blocks inside nested bullets, too.

    1. Like this:

      printf("Hello, World!");

    2. The key is to indent your fenced block in the same line as the first character of the line.

By default, it does not display line numbers. If you want to display line numbers for every code block, you can set kramdown.syntax_highlighter_opts.block.line_numbers to true in your _config.yml file.

If you want to display line numbers for a specific code block, all you have to do is wrap your code in a liquid tag:

{% highlight c++ linenos %}
code code code
{% endhighlight %}
